Ploty Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Płoty, Poland

Demolished. Until at least 1812, Płoty's Jewish community had no cemetery of its own and buried its dead a day's journey away in Stargard; even an 1820s request to hire a local gravedigger was denied. This cemetery, likely established sometime after 1812, also served the Jewish communities of Gołczewo and Gryfice before they established their own burial grounds. The last known burial took place in 1940; a woman interviewed by ESJF surveyors, who grew up playing near the cemetery as a girl, recalled it as totally destroyed even in her youth, with an apartment block eventually built on the site around 1990–91.
